rows.stem: Which of the following structures is well-developed in a mature seed of black pepper ?

options.label: A
options.text: Perisperm

options.label: B
options.text: Thalamus

options.label: C
options.text: Sepals

options.label: D
options.text: Peduncle

rows.solution: In most seeds the nucellus is used up during the development of the embryo and endosperm. In a few seeds, such as **black pepper** and beet, remnants of the nucellus persist in the mature seed as a well-developed layer called the **perisperm**. The thalamus, sepals and peduncle are parts of the flower or fruit, not of the seed. So the answer is option (A) Perisperm.

rows.stem:
Observe the following line diagram depicting the 28 days menstrual cycle of a healthy young woman.
Select the option of days on which this woman would be most and least fertile.

options.label: A
options.text: Most fertile days: 14 – 21; Least fertile days: 1 – 7

options.label: B
options.text: Most fertile days: 10 – 17; Least fertile days: 21 – 28

options.label: C
options.text: Most fertile days: 1 – 7; Least fertile days: 14 – 21

options.label: D
options.text: Most fertile days: 21 – 28; Least fertile days: 7 – 14

rows.figureNote: REQUIRED:a horizontal arrowed day axis ticked at 1, 7, 14, 21 and 28 (days), with a vertical line rising at day 1 captioned 'Menstruation' and another at day 14 captioned 'Ovulation'. The drawing gives the premise (where ovulation falls), not the answer, so it is described in full. Page idx 4.
rows.solution:
CBSE accepted both 'most fertile 14 – 21, least fertile 1 – 7' and 'most fertile 10 – 17, least fertile 21 – 28' for this question.

The diagram marks menstruation on day 1 and **ovulation on day 14** of the 28-day cycle. Fertilisation is possible only when sperms and the ovum meet in the fallopian tube, and both survive only for a limited time: the ovum for about a day after it is released and sperms for a few days. So the chances of fertilisation are highest in the days just before and just after ovulation. NCERT gives this period as **day 10 to day 17** of the cycle, which is why couples practising periodic abstinence avoid coitus on these days. Towards the end of the cycle (days 21 to 28) the ovum released on day 14 is no longer viable and no new ovum is released, so the chances of conception are lowest.

The pairing of days 14 to 21 with days 1 to 7 was also credited, as days 14 and 15 do fall in the fertile window and fertility is low during menstruation, but most of days 14 to 21 come after the ovum has ceased to be viable. So the answer is option (B) Most fertile days: 10 – 17; Least fertile days: 21 – 28.

rows.stem: Which one of the following was not present during the Mesozoic Era of the geological time scale ?

options.label: A
options.text: Ferns

options.label: B
options.text: Horsetails

options.label: C
options.text: Ginkgos

options.label: D
options.text: Bryophytes

rows.solution:
[CBSE marking scheme: bryophytes are keyed as the group absent from the Mesozoic. Strictly, bryophytes arose in the Palaeozoic Era and survive to this day, so they were also present in the Mesozoic; the key treats them, the oldest and simplest land plants in the list, as the odd one out.]

The Mesozoic Era (Triassic, Jurassic and Cretaceous periods) was the age of the gymnosperms and the dinosaurs. **Ferns** and **horsetails**, which had formed the great forests of the Carboniferous, continued into the Mesozoic, and **ginkgos**, along with cycads and conifers, were widespread during it. Bryophytes are the earliest land plants and belong to the beginning of the plant record, which is why the scheme selects them. So the answer is option (D) Bryophytes.

rows.stem: Identify the element used by Hershey and Chase to label the protein in their experiment, from the following options :
rows.solution: Hershey and Chase grew bacteriophages on a medium containing radioactive isotopes so that the virus coat and the virus DNA could be traced separately. Proteins contain **sulphur** (in amino acids such as cysteine and methionine) but no phosphorus, while DNA contains **phosphorus** but no sulphur. So the protein coat was labelled with radioactive sulphur, \(\text{S}^{35}\), and the DNA with radioactive phosphorus, \(\text{P}^{32}\). \(\text{S}^{32}\) is ordinary, non-radioactive sulphur and cannot be traced. So the answer is option (C) \(\text{S}^{35}\).

rows.stem: Which one among the following regions is not a hotspot of biodiversity ?

options.label: A
options.text: The Indo-Burma Region

options.label: B
options.text: Jaintia Hills in Meghalaya

options.label: C
options.text: The Western Ghats and Sri Lanka

options.label: D
options.text: The Himalayas

rows.solution: A **biodiversity hotspot** is a region with very high species richness and a high degree of endemism. Of the 34 hotspots of the world, three cover India's regions of exceptionally high biodiversity: the **Western Ghats and Sri Lanka**, **Indo-Burma** and the **Himalaya**. The **Jaintia Hills** (with the Khasi Hills) of Meghalaya are known instead for their **sacred groves**, tracts of forest protected by local communities for religious reasons, which is a form of in situ conservation, not a hotspot. So the answer is option (B) Jaintia Hills in Meghalaya.

rows.stem:
Assertion (A) : The Covid-19 virus has a shorter life-span and evolves into new strains at a fast speed.
Reason (R) : RNA being unstable, mutates at a faster rate.
rows.context: For Questions number 13 to 16, two statements are given — one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason (R). Select the correct answer to these questions from the codes (A), (B), (C) and (D) as given below.

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

rows.solution: RNA is chemically more reactive than DNA because of the 2'-OH group on every nucleotide, so it is **unstable** and **mutates at a faster rate**. Viruses that have an RNA genome and a short life span therefore mutate and evolve faster. The Covid-19 virus (SARS-CoV-2) is an RNA virus, and it has repeatedly given rise to new strains (variants) within a short time, so the Assertion is true. The Reason, that unstable RNA mutates quickly, is exactly why such a virus throws up new strains so fast. So both the Assertion and the Reason are true and the Reason is the correct explanation of the Assertion, which is option (A).

rows.stem:
Assertion (A) : For DNA sequencing, the total DNA from a cell is isolated and converted into random fragments of relatively smaller sizes.
Reason (R) : Human genome is said to have approximately \(3 \times 10^{9}\) bp and the total estimated cost for sequencing is very high.
rows.context: For Questions number 13 to 16, two statements are given — one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason (R). Select the correct answer to these questions from the codes (A), (B), (C) and (D) as given below.

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

rows.solution:
In the Human Genome Project the total DNA from a cell was isolated and converted into **random fragments of relatively smaller sizes**, which were cloned in suitable hosts (using BAC and YAC vectors) and then sequenced. This was necessary because DNA sequencers can read only short stretches of DNA at a time. The Assertion is true.

The human genome has approximately \(3 \times 10^{9}\) bp, and at an estimated cost of 3 US dollars per bp the total cost of sequencing came to about 9 billion US dollars, so the Reason is also true. But the size and cost explain why the project was a mega project, not why the DNA is broken into small fragments, which is a technical requirement of sequencing. So both the Assertion and the Reason are true, but the Reason is not the correct explanation of the Assertion, which is option (B).

rows.subtopic: Species Numbers and Patterns of Biodiversity
rows.stem:
Assertion (A) : Biologists are sure about how many prokaryotic species are living now.
Reason (R) : The conventional taxonomic methods are not suitable for identifying microbial species.
rows.context: For Questions number 13 to 16, two statements are given — one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason (R). Select the correct answer to these questions from the codes (A), (B), (C) and (D) as given below.

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

rows.solution: Biologists are **not sure** how many prokaryotic species there might be, so the Assertion is false. The reason for this uncertainty is that **conventional taxonomic methods are not suitable for identifying microbial species**, and many species are simply not culturable under laboratory conditions. If biochemical or molecular criteria are used to delineate species, their diversity alone might run into millions. So the Reason is true. So the Assertion is false while the Reason is true, which is option (D).

rows.stem:
Assertion (A) : Mary Mallon continued to spread typhoid for many years.
Reason (R) : Salmonella typhi generally enters the small intestine through food and water contaminated with it.
rows.context: For Questions number 13 to 16, two statements are given — one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason (R). Select the correct answer to these questions from the codes (A), (B), (C) and (D) as given below.

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

rows.solution:
Mary Mallon, nicknamed **Typhoid Mary**, was a cook who was a **carrier** of typhoid: she carried the bacterium without falling ill and continued to spread typhoid for several years through the food she prepared. So the Assertion is true. Typhoid is caused by **Salmonella typhi**, which generally enters the small intestine through **food and water contaminated** with it and migrates to other organs through the blood. So the Reason is also true, and it gives the route by which Mary Mallon infected the people who ate her food. So both the Assertion and the Reason are true and the Reason is the correct explanation of the Assertion, which is option (A).

(The key turns on the route of spread. What allowed her to go on spreading the disease for years was that she was a healthy carrier, which the Reason does not mention, so a reader who looks for that point may read the Reason as true but not the explanation.)

rows.stem:
(a) Name the two institutes which developed the technology of biogas production in India.
(b) Explain the main principle used in this technology.
rows.solution:
(a) The technology of biogas production in India was developed mainly through the efforts of the **Indian Agricultural Research Institute (IARI)** and the **Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC)**.

(b) The principle is the anaerobic breakdown of cellulosic material by **methanogens**:
- Methanogens such as Methanobacterium grow **anaerobically** on cellulosic material, for example the cattle dung (gobar) fed into a biogas plant.
- They produce a large amount of **methane** along with \(\text{CO}_2\) and \(\text{H}_2\); this mixture of gases is **biogas**.
- Biogas has a high calorific value and is used as a fuel for cooking and lighting, while the spent slurry is used as a fertiliser.

rows.stem: On August 22 in the year 2022, 3358 fires were detected in the Amazon rainforests. Write one short-term and one long-term effect of this event on the biotic and abiotic components of the environment.
rows.solution:
Large forest fires such as those in the Amazon affect both the living (biotic) and non-living (abiotic) components of the ecosystem.

- **Short-term effect:** the **death of plants and animals** and the immediate **loss of habitat and food**, especially for animals (including migratory ones) that depend on the forest; on the abiotic side, loss of green cover and **air pollution** from smoke, ash and the carbon dioxide released.
- **Long-term effect:** **fragmentation of the habitat** and **decline of populations**, so that important links in food chains disappear, leading to imbalances in biodiversity and even extinction of species; on the abiotic side, soil erosion and loss of soil fertility, and a rise in atmospheric carbon dioxide that adds to global warming.

The Amazon rain forest harbours probably millions of species, so its loss on this scale is a serious threat to biodiversity.

rows.stem: Trace the journey of a zygote from the isthmus of the fallopian tube up to its implantation in the uterus of a human female. Highlight the changes the zygote undergoes during the course of its journey up to implantation.
rows.solution:
Fertilisation takes place in the **ampullary region** of the fallopian tube, and the zygote then moves through the **isthmus** of the tube towards the uterus.
- As it moves, the zygote divides by **mitosis**; this division is called **cleavage**, and it forms 2, 4, 8 and 16 daughter cells called **blastomeres**.
- The embryo with 8 to 16 blastomeres is called a **morula**.
- The morula continues to divide and transforms into a **blastocyst** as it moves further into the uterus.
- The blastomeres in the blastocyst are arranged into an outer layer called the **trophoblast** and an inner group of cells attached to it called the **inner cell mass**.
- The trophoblast layer then gets attached to the **endometrium**, and the inner cell mass gets differentiated as the embryo.
- After attachment, the uterine cells divide rapidly and cover the blastocyst, so that it becomes embedded in the endometrium of the uterus. This is called **implantation**, and it leads to pregnancy.

The marking scheme also accepts a labelled diagram of the same journey, showing the zygote, the 2-cell stage, the morula, the blastocyst moving down the oviduct and the blastocyst implanted in the uterine wall.

rows.stem:
(i) Describe the arrangement of nuclei and cells in a mature embryo sac of a typical angiosperm.
(ii) Explain the devices the flowering plants have developed to prevent the following types of pollination :
(1) Prevents both autogamy and geitonogamy
(2) Prevents autogamy, but not geitonogamy
rows.solution:
(i) A mature angiosperm embryo sac is **7-celled and 8-nucleate**. It develops from the functional megaspore, whose nucleus divides mitotically three times (free nuclear divisions) to give 8 nuclei, after which cell walls are laid down. The cells are arranged as follows:
- **Egg apparatus** at the **micropylar end**: three cells grouped together, namely **two synergids** (which carry special cellular thickenings at the micropylar tip, the **filiform apparatus**, that guide the pollen tube) and **one egg cell**.
- **Antipodals**: three cells at the **chalazal end**.
- **Central cell**: the large seventh cell in the middle, containing **two polar nuclei**.

So 6 of the 8 nuclei are enclosed in cells of their own (egg, 2 synergids, 3 antipodals), while the 2 polar nuclei share the central cell. The marking scheme also accepts a labelled diagram showing the chalazal end, antipodals, polar nuclei, central cell, egg, synergids and micropylar end.

(ii) Flowering plants have developed several outbreeding devices:
- (1) **Prevents both autogamy and geitonogamy:** production of unisexual flowers, with male and female flowers on **different plants** (**dioecy**), as in papaya; a plant then cannot pollinate itself at all. **Self-incompatibility**, a genetic mechanism that prevents self-pollen from fertilising the ovules by inhibiting pollen germination or pollen tube growth in the pistil, also prevents both.
- (2) **Prevents autogamy but not geitonogamy:** production of unisexual flowers with male and female flowers on the **same plant** (**monoecy**), as in castor and maize; pollen cannot reach a stigma of the same flower, but it can reach a female flower of the same plant. In other species the pollen release and stigma receptivity are **not synchronised**, or the **anther and stigma are placed at different positions**, which also prevent pollen from reaching the stigma of the same flower.

rows.stem:
(i) Write the specific location of the following in the testis in humans :
(1) Sertoli cells
(2) Leydig cells
(ii) Explain the coordination between Gonadotropins, Leydig cells and Sertoli cells and their role in spermatogenesis.
rows.solution:
(i) Location in the human testis:
- (1) **Sertoli cells** lie **within the seminiferous tubules**, in the inner lining along with the male germ cells (spermatogonia); they provide nutrition to the germ cells.
- (2) **Leydig cells** (interstitial cells) lie in the **interstitial spaces between the seminiferous tubules**, outside them.

(ii) Spermatogenesis starts at puberty because of a significant increase in the secretion of **gonadotropin releasing hormone (GnRH)** by the hypothalamus.
- GnRH acts on the **anterior pituitary** gland and stimulates the secretion of two gonadotropins, **luteinising hormone (LH)** and **follicle stimulating hormone (FSH)**.
- **LH acts on the Leydig cells** and stimulates the synthesis and secretion of **androgens** (testosterone), which in turn stimulate the process of **spermatogenesis**.
- **FSH acts on the Sertoli cells** and stimulates the secretion of some factors which help in the process of **spermiogenesis** (the transformation of spermatids into sperms).

So the hypothalamus, the anterior pituitary, the Leydig cells and the Sertoli cells act as one chain: the gonadotropins from the pituitary drive the two kinds of testis cells, and the products of those cells (androgens and the Sertoli cell factors) bring about the formation of sperms. The marking scheme also accepts this as a flow chart: GnRH, acting on the anterior pituitary, gives LH and FSH; LH acts on the Leydig cells, which secrete androgens that stimulate spermatogenesis; FSH acts on the Sertoli cells, which release factors that stimulate spermiogenesis.
